feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Soaring living costs have many Nigerian couples rethinking the lavish wedding tradition
entry.summary: Nigeria's lavish wedding tradition is colliding with a cost-of-living crisis, forcing young couples to rethink how they say "I do."

entry.title: An emergency dig is on to recover displaced artifacts in Alaska before the next storm
entry.summary: During Typhoon Halong in 2025, thousands of objects from an archeological dig site in western Alaska were torn from the earth and scattered across miles of coastline. Now, there's an emergency dig.

entry.title: Understanding the importance of the White House press pool
entry.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with Bloomberg's Jeff Mason, past president of the White House Correspondents' Association about President Trump's decision to ban three major news outlets from the building.

entry.title: A 16-year-old thought he was going to die in a burning a car. Then a trucker appeared
entry.summary: A 16-year-old fell asleep at the wheel while on a hunting trip with his dad. Pinned in the wreckage with a fire starting, he thought he was going to die -- until a trucker pulled over to help.

entry.title: Remembering Chad Gilbert, guitarist of New Found Glory
entry.summary: New Found Glory guitarist Chad Gilbert died recently, after a battle with cancer. NPR remembers the founding member of the punk rock bank.

entry.title: Trump's big weekend: The arch, Greenland, and media outlets banned from White House
entry.summary: President Trump's exertion of power over the press, Greenland and even the D.C. landscape are teeing up questions over the president's limits.

entry.title: Washington press corps rallies around CNN, MS Now and Politico after White House ban
entry.summary: CNN, MS Now, and Politico are suing the Trump administration after being barred from the White House. Other TV networks are boycotting the White House press pool in solidarity.

entry.title: Journalist John Dickerson talks about his relationship to death
entry.summary: On Wild Card, famous guests open up about topics we don't often talk about. Journalist John Dickerson talks about his relationship to death.

entry.title: In conversation with 'the most normal guy in Hollywood' — Weird Al
entry.summary: After decades of making parody music, Weird Al has new generations of fans. His Tiny Desk Concert saw an audience of people in their 60s and kids who could have been their grandchildren.

entry.title: 'Washington Post' finds discrepancies in Iran war death numbers
entry.summary: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Tara Copp of The Washington Post about her reporting on the Defense Department's accounting of U.S. troops who've died over the course of the war with Iran.
